t: Rastas worship one God, Jah, whom they hold to be present within each individual; they accord key importance to Haile Selassie, whom many see as the Second Coming of Jesus and Jah incarnate and others as a human prophet.

Rastafari is Afrocentric: it teaches that the African diaspora lives in exile in "Babylon", meaning Western society, and many Rastas look to Africa as "Zion", although since the 1980s many understand the return in a metaphorical sense.

There is no central authority, no creed and no professional priesthood. Rastas call their practices "livity", and the movement is divided into "mansions", of which the Nyabinghi, the Bobo Ashanti and the Twelve Tribes of Israel are the most prominent.
dyk: Many Rastas speak of "knowing" Jah rather than "believing" in him, and they use "I" in place of "me", "I and I" in place of "we" and "downpression" in place of "oppression", because oppression bears down on people rather than lifting them up.
ev: Haile Selassie is crowned Emperor of Ethiopia, and several Jamaican clergymen claim that it fulfils biblical prophecy and shows that he is a black messiah
Jamaica's colonial authorities arrest Leonard Howell and charge him with sedition, and he is imprisoned for two years
Howell forms a Rasta community known as Pinnacle in Saint Catherine Parish, which the police raid repeatedly and which closes in 1954
After the first Rastafarian Universal Convention in Back-o-Wall, Kingston, Rasta militants unsuccessfully try to capture the city in Haile Selassie's name
Haile Selassie visits Jamaica at its government's invitation, and thousands of Rastas gather to see his arrival at the airport
Haile Selassie dies a year after his overthrow by the Derg, which causes a crisis of faith for many practitioners
The first international assembly of Rastafari groups takes place in Toronto, Canada
Jamaica decriminalises personal possession of marijuana up to two ounces

f.origin: Jamaica, in the 1930s, among impoverished and socially disenfranchised Afro-Jamaican communities, after clergymen proclaimed that Haile Selassie's 1930 crowning as Emperor of Ethiopia fulfilled biblical prophecy.
f.founder: none: there is no single founder and no leader followed by all Rastafari. Early preachers who proclaimed Haile Selassie the returned Jesus included Leonard Howell, Archibald Dunkley, Robert Hinds and Joseph Hibbert, and Howell was the early movement's leading figure.
f.scriptures: The Bible, often read literally and as cryptographic, with the Book of Revelation seen as especially important; also Leonard Howell's The Promised Key (1935), Robert Athlyi Rogers' Holy Piby (1924), Fitz Balintine Pettersburg's Royal Parchment Scroll of Black Supremacy (1920s) and, for many Rastas, the 14th-century Ethiopian Kebra Nagast.
f.followers: An estimated 700,000 to 1,000,000 worldwide in 2012; 29,026 people identified as Rastas in Jamaica's 2011 census, and about 5,000 in England and Wales in the 2001 census.
